name: manual_923cae
claim: Before making a change on any branch, explicitly confirm the current checkout matches the branch the change is actually meant for -- run a quick identity check (branch name, or the tip commit's short SHA) rather than assuming the last `git checkout` succeeded in spirit as well as literally. When work spans two related repos or two related branches in the same repo, switching context (even briefly, to check something in the other repo) is exactly when this assumption silently breaks -- the same mistake (editing a shared policy file on a `main`-based branch instead of the actual feature branch) recurred twice in immediate succession within one session, the second time in the very same class of file the first mistake was about.

decisions.notes: The mistake recurred within the same session even after being caught once -- worth a durable, explicit lesson, not just a one-time fix.

rationale: The mistake recurred within the same session even after being caught once -- worth a durable, explicit lesson, not just a one-time fix.
